your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Maintain three houses on both monopolies; no further optional spending. $48 cash plus $425 mortgage capacity on spare assets covers near-term liabilities. Avoid trading opponents complete sets; Claude approaches dark blues and Grok approaches light blues.

Buy for $260, leaving $959. Denies Claude the remaining yellow and adds mortgage capacity without meaningful liquidity risk. Next priority: activate oranges ($308 unmortgage plus $900 for three houses each), with light-blue upgrades an immediate cheap option as Claude approaches.

Claude is on Mediterranean, immediately approaching light blues. $150 raises rents to $400/$400/$450 and leaves $809. Next activate oranges for $308 and fund nine houses ($900) with spare-property mortgages; 11 bank houses remain, enough. His weak pinks pose little risk.

Activate oranges: $308 total unmortgaging plus $900 for nine houses. Current $809 plus $555 spare mortgage capacity leaves $156 reserve. Nine orange houses also exhaust most bank supply, limiting Claude's pink development.

Continue activating orange monopoly: Tennessee $99, New York $110, then nine houses $900. Current $709 plus $555 idle-property mortgage capacity covers all with $155 reserve; pink rents only $50–70. Preserve light-blue and dark-blue buildings.

Unmortgage New York for $110, leaving $499. Mortgage idle Atlantic ($130), Illinois ($120), Water Works ($75), Baltic ($30), and railroads as needed to fund nine orange houses for $900 with reserve. Opponent near light blues then oranges; accelerate third rent engine and house lock.

Mortgage idle Atlantic for $130, bringing cash to $628. Need $900 for three houses per orange; mortgage Illinois, Water Works, and one railroad next to retain ~$123. Opponent approaches our light blues and oranges; prioritize rent engines and house scarcity.

Mortgage isolated Illinois for $120, reaching $748. Then Water Works ($75) and one railroad ($100) fund nine orange houses with $123 cash reserve. Three strong rent engines and house scarcity should finish Claude.

Mortgage Water Works for $75 to reach $823, then Short Line for $100. Build three houses on each orange for $900, leaving $123 and two bank houses; opponent's pink development constrained. Keep Reading active for $25 rents.

Mortgage Short Line to reach $923, then build three houses per orange for $900. Keep $23 plus $130 remaining mortgage capacity; weak opposing pink rents make this safe. Prior notes incorrectly computed $123 reserve; actual is $23. Nine houses leave just two in bank and deny pink upgrades.

message.reasoning:
With $144 to p2's $23, and only 2 houses left in the bank, I'm considering snapping those up just to create a housing shortage and block p2's strong board — their light blues at 4 houses could hotel soon, which would free up houses again, while their oranges and purple/baby-blue sets sit at 3 each.

Building would mean mortgaging a railroad to get to $244, leaving only $44 after construction, which is risky if I land on p2's oranges and can't pay. But p2's own cash position is so thin that a modest rent hit — even at 1-2 houses — would likely force them to sell buildings back to the bank, so keeping cash liquid and letting their fragile finances do the work may be smarter than overextending myself right now.
